title: Data import
description:
Day imports source changes without loss or duplicate records.

Planned verification cases: Changed event duration, late events, out-of-order events, crashes, and restart.

title: Tmux watcher
description:
The watcher identifies the active terminal project.

Planned verification cases: Two clients, two panes, window changes, detached sessions, and secret command arguments.

title: Read API
description:
The website receives consistent data through bounded API requests.

Planned verification cases: API access control, response format, and a repeatable performance test.

title: Time rules
description:
All sources use the same rules for intervals and duration.

Planned verification cases: Overlaps, adjacent intervals, midnight, daylight saving time, clock errors, and simultaneous devices.

title: Measurement rules
description:
Each metric has an explicit definition and shows missing data.

Planned verification cases: The calculation examples below, zero duration, missing data, and a changed plan.

Accepted task time means non-idle time with an accepted attribution to the task. The minimum qualifying task duration is undecided. Coverage threshold proposal: 90%.

title: Data history and recovery
description:
The user can inspect, restore, and delete personal records.

Planned verification cases: Backup restoration, deletion with recalculation, and repository checks.

title: Calendar
description:
The user can see local and imported events in one calendar.

Planned verification cases: Event changes, recurrence, daylight saving time, reminders, duplicates, and conflicts.

title: Tasks
description:
The user can capture tasks, connect goals, and set priorities.

Planned verification cases: All five categories, valid goal links, source changes, and historical references.

title: Goals
description:
Day can read personal goals and their criteria from Coherence.

Planned verification cases: Separate catalogs and an unavailable Coherence service.

title: Activity records
description:
Watchers record supported activity without repeated questions to the user.

Planned verification cases: Foreground activity, background activity, idle time, permissions, and capture pauses.

title: Attribution
description:
Day connects observations to tasks and records the reason for each connection.

Planned verification cases: Rule matches, conflicts, corrections, and an incorrect agent suggestion.

title: Charts and history
description:
The user can inspect activity and progress over different periods.

Planned verification cases: Interval totals, period boundaries, daylight saving time, and matching chart and table values.

title: Notes and experiments
description:
The user can save personal notes beside activity data and experiment results.

Planned verification cases: Note creation, changes, deletion, access control, and period comparisons.

title: CLI and agents
description:
Users and agents operate Day through the same commands.

Planned verification cases: JSON output, noninteractive execution, repeated requests, and access control.

title: Setup and services
description:
The user can install Day and open it through local HTTPS.

Planned verification cases: First setup, repeated setup, restart, isolated CI, and deployment checks.

title: Tutorial
description:
Each tutorial step produces a result that the user can see.

Planned verification cases: An interrupted tutorial and a manual check on a second screen.

title: Review a day
description:
The user can see where observed time went and which goals it helped.

Planned verification cases: Two tasks, one meeting, overlapping watchers, and a watcher outage.

title: Review personal experiments
description:
The user can save hypotheses and compare results over time.

Planned verification cases: An experiment with incomplete baseline data and a manual review of the comparison.

title: Complete the first task cycle
description:
A new user can connect a goal, task, session, observation, and result.

Planned verification cases: An automated integration test and a recorded manual tutorial.

title: Show the daily plan
description:
The user can keep tasks and events visible on another screen.

Planned verification cases: Three screen widths, a source update, connection loss, and read-only API access.

title: Connect plans and work
description:
Each work session connects a task, a calendar block, and a result.

Planned verification cases: Session operations, adapter failures, and repeated requests.

title: Check goals
description:
Day can repeat a goal check from saved data and definitions.

Planned verification cases: Repeated calculation, a changed rule, and a correctly calculated missed target.

title: Keep personal data local
description:
Day stores and processes personal data locally unless the user enables a specific transfer.

Planned verification cases: Offline operation, export exclusions, disabled transfers, and access control.

title: Reconcile mutable events
intent: Import identifies an event by source, bucket, and event ID. Changed data or duration updates the existing copy without a duplicate observation.

title: Recover late data
intent: After restart, import recovers late events and duration changes through an overlap window or equivalent check. The checkpoint advances only after committed storage.

title: Expose failure
intent: After repeated adapter errors, Day keeps the last successful checkpoint. It marks the source stale and shows retry status.

title: Identify the pane
intent: Each observation identifies host, tmux client, session, window, pane, timestamp, and working directory or configured project ID.

title: Gate on foreground context
intent: Detached sessions and background clients do not receive foreground attribution. If Day cannot connect a terminal window to its client, it reports unknown context.

title: Avoid content capture
intent: Default observations exclude terminal contents, shell history, and command arguments.

title: Return a consistent snapshot
intent: A dashboard response includes timezone, interval, snapshot and evaluation revision, source update times, calendar, task groups, and metrics.

title: Bound history queries
intent: Raw-event queries require a bounded interval and pagination. Summary queries return calculated period data, not a year of raw events.

title: Stay responsive
intent: For cached day and week requests, p95 response time is below 500 ms over 100 requests. The test uses a synthetic one-year dataset on a documented local machine.

title: Use half-open intervals
intent: Stored intervals use UTC and include their start but exclude their end: `[start, end)`. Display periods use an IANA timezone, initially `Europe/Warsaw`.

title: Bound totals
intent: Day clips intervals to the requested period. It combines overlaps before calculating duration. Total attributed time cannot exceed observed non-idle time.

title: Resolve cross-device overlap
intent: For simultaneous device activity, Day applies an explicit device-selection rule or marks the interval ambiguous. It does not add simultaneous durations together.

title: Reject invalid timing
intent: Day excludes negative durations and impossible timestamps from calculations. It retains invalid records separately with reasons. Clock errors remain visible.

title: Define denominator
intent: Session adherence is accepted task time within the planned interval divided by planned work time. Breaks scheduled before work are outside that interval. Zero planned duration returns unavailable.

title: Expose coverage
intent: Coverage is the fraction of planned work time with known activity or idle state from the required watchers. Day shows coverage separately from adherence. Missing data is not idle time or unrelated work.

title: Gate a decision
intent: A session needs the configured coverage threshold for a conclusive adherence result. The proposed threshold is 90%. Below it, status is `insufficient_data`.

title: Prevent retrospective inflation
intent: A change to the planned duration of an ended session creates a new plan revision. The original plan and result remain visible.

title: Separate progress and time
intent: Day reports progress entries, result links, attributed time, and adherence separately. One value does not establish another.

title: Keep provenance
intent: Calculated records retain source references, algorithm and configuration revisions, and creation time. Attribution corrections do not change raw evidence.

title: Export and restore
intent: Local backup can restore source data, notes, adapter IDs, attributions, goals, and evaluation history into a separate installation. Record counts and checksums match.

title: Apply deletion
intent: Deletion removes selected personal content and invalidates dependent results. Any retained history identifies the deletion without retaining deleted content. Day explains the effect on backups.

title: Keep private runtime files out of Git
intent: Repository checks reject tracked credentials, live stores, private notes, and raw activity data. Examples use synthetic records.

title: Manage local blocks
intent: The CLI can create, change, and cancel local blocks. Changes preserve the event ID. The API shows the resulting interval.

title: Preserve time semantics
intent: Events retain timezone, all-day, and recurrence information. A change to one occurrence does not change the series unless the user requests it.

title: Sync predictably
intent: Google synchronization creates no duplicate for an unchanged external revision. Day records deletions and shows concurrent changes as conflicts for resolution.

title: Preserve reminders
intent: Imported events retain their reminder settings. Local blocks can request reminders. Day shows when the selected source cannot deliver a reminder.

title: Capture before sorting
intent: A title alone creates an inbox task with a stable ID. Goal, urgency, and importance remain unset.

title: Categorize explicitly
intent: A task with both urgency and importance set appears in exactly one of the four priority categories. Other tasks stay in inbox.

title: Bind a goal
intent: A task can reference multiple existing Coherence goals. A session requires a selected primary goal. Completed and cancelled tasks cannot start sessions.

title: Keep identities stable
intent: Day identifies source edits, completion, and cancellation by task ID. Source deletion does not remove historical session or progress references.

title: Resolve a goal reference
intent: A goal reference contains its catalog ID and spec ID. The adapter returns the goal title, ACs, status, and revision.

title: Keep catalogs distinct
intent: Software specifications and personal goals use separate catalogs. Tests use a third, disposable catalog.

title: Handle unavailable goals
intent: If Coherence is unavailable, Day marks cached goals stale. It blocks new links that it cannot check. Existing history remains available.

title: Capture supported context
intent: Observations identify the foreground application and supported active browser tab. When the terminal is foreground, observations include its active tmux pane and project.

title: Distinguish presence from activity
intent: Background tabs, detached tmux sessions, and inactive panes do not add foreground time merely because they are open.

title: Show collection limits
intent: Day shows unsupported browsers, missing permissions, watcher failures, and capture pauses. The coverage view identifies their affected intervals.

title: Pause and exclude
intent: The user can pause capture or exclude sensitive contexts. Exclusion occurs before data storage. Day retains the excluded interval without its content.

title: Apply explicit rules
intent: A rule can match a project path, tmux context, application, or URL pattern. Each assigned interval records the rule ID and version.

title: Leave ambiguity visible
intent: Conflicting matches with equal rank remain ambiguous until resolved. Observations without matches remain unassigned.

title: Correct without erasure
intent: A manual correction creates an attribution revision and reason. Source observations and earlier decisions remain unchanged.

title: Keep intent separate
intent: A running task or calendar block alone cannot assign concurrent activity to that task.

title: Bound generated suggestions
intent: Agent suggestions show observation IDs, method or model version, and uncertainty. Suggestions do not become accepted attributions until accepted.

title: Aggregate unique time
intent: Day counts each elapsed second at most once in totals. Overlapping events or multiple goal links cannot increase elapsed time.

title: Drill into a chart
intent: When the user selects a chart period, Day shows its intervals, coverage, attribution versions, and progress entries.

title: Render all requested periods
intent: Day supports day, week, month, quarter, and year views. Each view uses the same metric definitions and explicit local-time boundaries.

title: Display task priorities consistently
intent: All five task categories remain visible. Non-urgent tasks with low importance are gray but readable.

title: Capture a note
intent: The CLI saves note text and a timestamp. Task, goal, session, and experiment links are optional. Notes are private by default.

title: Preserve edits
intent: A note change preserves its earlier revision and author. Explicit deletion follows the deletion policy and removes data, not only its display.

title: Compare an experiment
intent: An experiment view shows the selected metric before and after a change, with related notes. It marks changed definitions and inadequate coverage.

title: Expose a coherent surface
intent: One CLI help tree lists task, calendar, goal, session, note, activity, report, service, and tutorial operations.

title: Support automation
intent: Data commands support `--json`. They send versioned results to stdout and diagnostics to stderr. Errors have stable codes and a nonzero exit status. Noninteractive commands do not wait for input.

title: Assemble task context
intent: A task context query returns state, goals, ACs, sessions, progress, related activity, source update times, and available next operations.

title: Retry safely
intent: Each data change accepts an operation ID. A repeated request returns the same record IDs without duplicate tasks, notes, or events.

title: Respect capability scope
intent: Read-only agent credentials cannot change data. Logs identify the actor and operation ID for each change.

title: Prepare
intent: `prepare` checks commands, versions, ports, environment variables, data paths, adapters, and Caddy requirements. It explains necessary corrections without secret values.

title: Set up safely
intent: `setup` creates the required configuration and stores. Repeated execution preserves existing data and IDs. It does not silently replace personal records with test data.

title: Isolate CI
intent: `ci` uses disposable stores and synthetic activity. It cannot change personal tasks, events, goals, or observations.

title: Manage service lifecycle
intent: `start`, `stop`, and `status` control application services and host watchers. Status shows each component. Stop preserves data.

title: Deploy locally
intent: `deploy` connects the application to the configured Caddy network. It checks the hostname and certificate trust from a target client. It runs authenticated HTTPS smoke tests. A failed check produces a failed deployment status.

title: Gate on reality
intent: Each tutorial step checks its saved result before the next step. The sequence checks service health, goal, task, block, observation, attribution, progress entry, and website result.

title: Use real observation
intent: The tracking step requires a real watcher event. A labelled demo mode can use synthetic events. Demo events cannot satisfy real-tracking completion.

title: Resume safely
intent: Tutorial progress survives restart. The tutorial reuses its existing records without duplicates.

title: End with tomorrow
intent: The final step shows the website URL, recorded result, and command to continue the same goal tomorrow.

title: Follow the evidence
intent: When the user selects an attributed interval, Day shows its task, goal, observations, attribution method, and progress entries.

title: Preserve uncertainty
intent: Day shows missing intervals separately from idle time, unassigned activity, and activity connected to goals.

title: Compare intent and observation
intent: Day shows planned blocks beside observed activity. Planned time does not count as observed work.

title: Record the hypothesis
intent: Before comparison, an experiment has a saved hypothesis, proposed change, observation period, and metric definition.

title: Inspect change
intent: The comparison shows baseline values, later values, coverage, metric versions, and related notes. Missing baseline data stays marked as unavailable.

title: Keep interpretation attributable
intent: Conclusions and suggestions show their author or method and timestamp. Day keeps them separate from measured values.

title: Obtain a real result
intent: The tutorial creates a goal, task, scheduled session, real observation, attribution, and progress entry. The deployed website shows these records together.

title: Resume tomorrow
intent: After restart, Day shows the saved goal, task state, last progress entry, and next command.

title: Observe user completion
intent: The user completes a manual tutorial without direct changes to adapter configuration files. The tutorial explains and requests necessary credentials.

title: Show the current situation
intent: The daily view shows the current time, calendar, current task, next event, and five task categories. It also shows source update times.

title: Support the target screens
intent: The current task and next event fit within widths of 390, 768, and 1440 CSS pixels without horizontal scroll. Calendar navigation remains usable.

title: Refresh without misleading
intent: Imported changes appear within 30 seconds when the connection works. If the connection fails, Day keeps the last view and marks it stale.

title: Keep the dashboard read-only
intent: The website has no controls to change tasks or events. Its read-only credentials cannot change data through the API.

title: Schedule a task
intent: When the user schedules a ready task with a valid goal and interval, Day creates one session and one connected calendar occurrence.

title: Start immediately
intent: For an unscheduled ready task, the user selects a duration. Day creates a block that starts now. The CLI shows the task, goal, planned end, and session ID.

title: Resolve collisions
intent: Before a session starts, Day shows any overlap with an appointment or running session. The user selects another interval or explicitly replaces the running session.

title: Close with progress
intent: When the user ends work, Day saves a status update and closes the session. A result link is optional. Task completion needs a separate action.

title: Recover interrupted writes
intent: If calendar creation fails after session creation, Day shows the incomplete operation. A retry with the same operation ID creates no duplicate block.

title: Snapshot the calculation
intent: Each evaluation records the goal revision, period, input snapshot IDs, attribution version, thresholds, and calculation version.

title: Expose the result
intent: Each evaluated AC shows a status, value, threshold, coverage, and evidence links. Status is `met`, `not_met`, or `insufficient_data`.

title: Preserve history
intent: A changed goal or attribution rule produces a new evaluation revision. Earlier results remain available.

title: Separate software and life results
intent: If Day correctly calculates a missed personal target, the software test passes. The personal target stays `not_met`.

title: Operate without cloud services
intent: After installation, local functions work without external services. This includes plans, activity records, attribution, notes, evaluation, and the website. Google synchronization and remote inference must be disabled for this check.

title: Separate public output
intent: Public export includes only records selected for publication. Default exclusions include private notes, raw URLs, window titles, credentials, and live data files.

title: Scope optional transfers
intent: Before an external integration starts, Day shows its destination and data categories. When disabled, it stops transfers. Local functions continue to work.

title: Restrict access
intent: LAN clients without authentication cannot read private activity or notes. The dashboard proxy does not expose the ActivityWatch service.
